name: Table
intent: A semantic table of rows and columns, like invoices or accounts, with optional row selection, a caption and a total.
usage: Use Table for lists of records. It is one component: pass columns and rows as data. Headers are kit HeaderCells; string and number values become text Cells, and anything richer is a kit Cell you put in the row (badge, avatar, link, actionMenu). Number columns take numeric, which aligns them to the end with even digits. selectable adds a checkbox column: each row gets a checkbox Cell and the header a select-all that shows a dash when only some rows are picked. The caption sits under the grid; footer holds a total in the last column. With no rows, one cell spans the columns and shows emptyLabel. Search, filters and actions belong in a Toolbar above it. Every cell keeps its value on one line at any width, so a name, a contract, a date or an amount never wraps down its cell; when the columns need more room than the box has, the table grows wider than its box and scrolls sideways inside it. The table answers to the width of its own box: under 640px, the kit's mobile break, the first column is frozen against the start edge while the rest of the row slides under it; with selectable, the checkbox column is frozen with it, so a row can still be ticked while it is read. For parent and child rows, put a Cell type tree in the first column and list only the rows whose parents are open. See contracts/table.json for the full contract.

columns.itemShape: { key: string; header?: string; align?: "start" | "center" | "end"; numeric?: boolean; emphasis?: boolean; width?: string }
columns.note: key picks the row value. numeric aligns to the end with tabular digits. emphasis makes the column's text medium weight, like the record id. width is a CSS width, like 30%.

rows.note: One object per row, keyed by column key. Strings and numbers become text Cells; pass a kit Cell for anything else. id identifies the row for selection; it defaults to the row's index.

size.note: Row height 48 / 56, header 40 / 48, same as Cell and HeaderCell. Without a size, a surrounding Density in compact makes it sm. Give Cells you pass the same size.

caption.note: Describes the table. Sits under the grid, and names the table for screen readers.

footer.note: A total row: label across the first columns, value in the last column.

emptyLabel.note: Shown in one cell across the columns when rows is empty. Headers stay, so the table keeps its shape.

selectable.note: Adds a checkbox column with a select-all in the header.

selected.note: Controlled ids of the selected rows.

defaultSelected.note: Starting selection when selected is not controlled.

rowLabel.note: Column key whose value names each row checkbox, like Select INV001. Defaults to the first column.

onRowClick.note: Clicking anywhere on a row runs it, for picking a row, like in a Lookup. It is a pointer shortcut: give the row a keyboard control too, like a link Cell with onClick in its first column. Clicks on the row's own links, buttons and checkboxes act on their own.

useWhen: Records people scan, compare and pick from: invoices, accounts, products.
A short list of values with a total, like line items.
doNot: Do not invent TableHeader, TableRow, TableCell or a local grid of divs. Pass columns and rows.
Do not draw cell content yourself. Use kit Cell types for badges, people, links and row actions.
Do not put search or filters in the table. Use a Toolbar above it.
Do not wrap it in your own scrolling box or set a width on it to make it fit a phone. It scrolls sideways and freezes its first column on its own.
Do not force a wide table into a narrow column by letting values break mid-word. Give it the room, or let it scroll sideways in its own box.
a11y: A native table: caption, th scope=col headers (kit HeaderCell) and td cells. A column with no header, like row actions, gets a plain cell in the header row instead of an empty header.
Row checkboxes are named Select plus the row label; the header one is Select all rows and is mixed when only some rows are selected. Selected rows set aria-selected.
The empty message is a real cell spanning the columns, so screen readers read it in place.
On a narrow box the sideways scroll is the table's own box, so the page never scrolls sideways and the frozen first column keeps the row's name in view.
A table wider than its box scrolls sideways inside it; then the box is a focus stop named by caption (or Table), so the arrow keys scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1). When it fits, it adds no tab stop.
snippet:
<Table
  caption="A list of your recent invoices."
  columns={[
    { key: "invoice", header: "Invoice", emphasis: true },
    { key: "status", header: "Status" },
    { key: "method", header: "Method" },
    { key: "amount", header: "Amount", numeric: true },
  ]}
  rows={invoices}
  footer={{ label: "Total", value: "$2,500.00" }}
/>

examples.title: Invoices
examples.usage: Caption under the grid, the total in the footer, and Amount at the end of each row.

props.caption: A list of your recent invoices.

examples.title: Selection
examples.usage: selectable adds the checkbox column. Pick some rows and the header shows a dash; the header picks all or none.

examples.title: Rich cells
examples.usage: Put kit Cells in rows for status, people and row actions. Strings still become text Cells.

examples.title: Icon actions
examples.usage: A last column of icon-only row actions: a kit Cell with type actionIcons, up to three buttons. Each is named by its label, like Edit, and the group by Actions for INV001.

examples.title: Empty
examples.usage: No rows: one cell spans the columns and shows emptyLabel. Headers keep the shape.
